Cubic Bezier Generator

Design custom cubic-bezier() timing functions with sliders — live curve, handles and an animated preview ball.

📖 How to use

  1. Drag the X1/Y1/X2/Y2 sliders (or type exact values).
  2. Watch the curve, its control handles and the preview ball update live.
  3. Copy the cubic-bezier() snippet into your CSS transitions.

❓ Frequently asked questions

What do the four numbers mean?

The curve runs from (0,0) to (1,1). P1=(x1,y1) and P2=(x2,y2) are control points that bend it. X values must stay in 0–1 for CSS; Y can overshoot for bounce-like effects.

Why do presets matter?

Presets like ease-out-back encode well-tested motion feels. Start from one, then tweak the handles to taste.

Where do I paste the output?

Into transition-timing-function or the timing slot of the animation shorthand, e.g. transition: transform .4s cubic-bezier(.34,1.56,.64,1);
